name: neorgon-forge
description: Skills for finding your way into hard work, taking it on, and then explaining it: wayfind (a map of an unfamiliar codebase, and tickets resolved to files), untangle (a problem whose shape is not yet known), atlas (a dependency model, an MkDocs site generated from it, and answers you can check), task (scoped execution with delegated workstreams), debrief (the work as a deck), writeup (the work as a published post), deckcraft (a deck whose headings argue rather than name topics), voicecheck (copy that stays on-voice across projects), penname (new prose in English or Spanish, drafted under a corpus-derived persona, linted against checkable register rules, with a ledger of accepted corrections that outranks the persona), groundwork (a tutorial's prerequisites, credentials, and limits investigated and dated before the tutorial promises them), quizmaster (source material turned into a validated Proctor-format exam), mascot-forge (a generated character, cut out and rigged), secret-safe-reporting (reports about sensitive data that cannot leak it).

plugins.name: neorgon-forge
plugins.description: Thirteen skills, portable by default. wayfind and untangle come before the work: one maps a codebase you do not know, the other handles a problem whose shape is not yet known. atlas turns an app into a dependency model, then generates its diagrams and docs from that model so they go stale loudly rather than silently. task writes a brief while the work happens; debrief and writeup read it afterwards instead of reconstructing it from memory. deckcraft covers the deck that did not come from a diff: it writes the headings before the bullets, because a heading that names a subject cannot be disagreed with and so cannot carry an argument. voicecheck and mascot-forge cover the two things that drift fastest across a fleet of sites: how the copy reads and how the art holds together. penname, groundwork and quizmaster serve the writing itself: drafting under a persona whose register rules are checkable, investigating what a service requires before a tutorial promises it, and turning source material into a validated exam. secret-safe-reporting sits across all of it: pipelines that report on sensitive data without leaking it.
